summary.headline: Nuvama FY26 operating PAT crossed INR1,000 crore; Q4 operating PAT up 5% YoY to INR269 crore, with wealth and asset services driving growth.
summary.overview: Management reported a growth year despite a volatile FY26 marked by tariffs, the West Asia crisis and subdued capital markets. Wealth and Private grew operating PBT by about 22-24%, and asset services recovered after a Q1 decline to end FY26 with revenue up about 12%. Capital markets (IB and IE) softened, with QIP volumes down and ECM subdued in Q4. Q4 firm revenue was about INR825 crore (+7% YoY; +13% excluding IE and IB), and firm ROE was 28%. Management says Wealth and Private now contribute 55% of firm revenue, and wealth, asset management and asset services together about 80%.

segments.name: Nuvama Wealth
segments.commentary: Revenue INR960 crore (+18%). MPIS assets about INR39,000 crore, with net new money about INR8,900 crore (about 30% of opening MPIS assets). Retention about 90 bps. Loan book about INR4,900 crore (+27%). NII about 20-22% of revenue.

segments.name: Nuvama Private
segments.commentary: ARR assets about INR54,000 crore; ARR yield 1.00% in Q4, with management guiding an average of 90-95 bps. Lending is 10-12% of revenue. RM headcount rose from 90 to about 150 over four years. Operating PBT +24%.

segments.name: Asset Management
segments.commentary: Management fee income +31% YoY. Commercial real estate fund about INR3,800 crore raised by Q4, with the fund fully closed at about INR4,000 crore. Crossover 4 PE fund targets INR1,000-1,500 crore. Private credit first fund targets INR1,000-1,500 crore. Public markets roughly flat net flows.

segments.name: Asset Services
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR209 crore, above Q1 INR193 crore. FY26 revenue +12%, profit about +14-15%. Domestic RTA and trusteeship services expected live by mid-Q3 FY27. Global-local custodian tie-up on the verge of signing. Market share about 22% of chosen segments.

segments.name: Capital Markets (IB and IE)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR138 crore. Equity cash ADT -6%, futures ADT -14%, options +8% for FY26. IPO market share 19% by value and 15% by deals. Fixed income revenue +34-35% YoY, now about 50% of IB. IB/IE split about 30:70.

guidance_outlook: Asset services yields expected to hold at current levels; a possible rise over 12-15 months if inflation stays sticky and rates rise.
Wealth cost-to-income expected to fall about 100 bps a year over 3-4 years, with management choosing how much productivity gain to reinvest in RMs.
Private ARR yield expected to average 90-95 bps.
Management expects a good year in investment banking in FY27, with a 40-45 live mandate pipeline.
FY27 will carry incremental asset management costs for new strategies and the MF/SIF launch, which management calls investment rather than run-rate cost.
Bank guarantee norms expected to cost about INR10-15 crore a year net of deposit costs.
Private credit fund launch by end Q2 FY27; commercial real estate fund launch in H2 FY27 targeting INR3,000-3,500 crore (other remarks cite INR3,000-4,000 crore).
SIF launch expected after MF license, roughly two to three months from now.
capex_capacity: Commercial real estate fund: about INR3,800 crore raised by Q4; 40-50% deployed; three assets acquired (about 3.8 mn sq ft). New fund launch once about 70% deployed, expected H2 FY27.
Private equity Crossover 4 fund: about INR250-275 crore raised so far, target INR1,000-1,500 crore over the next 6-10 months.
Private credit: CIO Amit Kansal appointed; first fund targeting INR1,000-1,500 crore, launch by end Q2 FY27.
Virasat estate and legacy planning service launched; agentic AI tools deployed for RMs.
Asset services: RTA and trusteeship go-live expected by mid-Q3 FY27.
demand_pricing: Net flows in Wealth ran at 30% of opening MPIS assets; Private net flows about 22% of opening assets, in line with guidance.
Regret attrition: Private about 1-2%, Wealth about 3-4%. Management says AUM loss is limited.
Wealth RM productivity up about 25% YoY, helped by a lower share of under-one-year RMs (from 40-45% to about 33%) and AI tools. Private revenue per RM up 10-15% from agentic AI.
Private transactional revenue up 14% in FY26 vs ARR up 32%. Transactional revenue is about 90-95% broking and fixed income, with the rest deals.
Insurance volume growth moderated to about 25-30% from about 50%; management reports no yield impact. Category 2 mix may rise in volatile markets.
Industry view: new entrants offer high RM payouts, which management calls a caution; consolidation expected, with a few scale multiproduct leaders.
Mutual fund commission cut (April 1): management says impact negligible, as MF is under 20% of IE revenue and pass-through is similar to proposal.
Public markets: gross flows offset by redemptions, net flat for FY26.

qa_highlights.question: How should ECM revenue share be modelled for FY27 given large upcoming IPOs, and what is the impact of the MF commission cut?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cites 40-45 live ECM and advisory mandates, and Q4 deal slippage is expected to recover. MF commission cut impact is hardly material, as MF is under 20% of IE revenue and net margins are similar.

qa_highlights.question: Is the asset services yield at risk as rates fall, and what drove the higher cash share?
qa_highlights.answer: Yields should hold, as rate cuts have already flowed through. The cash share rose after a large client was replaced by many smaller clients; the portfolio mix is about 70:30 to 75:25. A rate hike would lift yields as deposits reprice.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 25% wealth productivity gain from AI or from mix, and how do clients per RM evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributes it to RM seasoning (under-one-year share fell to about 33%) plus AI tools. Net new money is the outcome, not the cause of productivity.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for transactional revenue in FY27 and the insurance commission trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Transactional revenue is mostly broking and fixed income, which are insulated from geopolitics. Insurance yields are steady, with some first-year commission support from category 2 products.

qa_highlights.question: How will cost-to-income ratios evolve in Wealth?
qa_highlights.answer: Wealth CTI fell 130-150 bps this year. Management guides about 100 bps a year over 3-4 years, with reinvestment in RM capacity as the lever.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27 asset management flow expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: PE Crossover 4 targets INR1,000-1,500 crore; private credit first fund INR1,000-1,500 crore with about half this year; CRE fund INR3,000-4,000 crore with 30-40% this year. SIF flow numbers to be discussed next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What share of the Ultra-HNI book sits above INR10 crore, and what is the mix of wealth clients by geography?
qa_highlights.answer: Families above INR10 crore are about one-third of the total and contribute 70-75% of AUM. Tier 2 and beyond is 35-40% of Nuvama Wealth. Private: top 8 cities about 80-85%.

risks_watch: Capital market revenue cyclicality: ECM and QIP volumes softened in H2 FY26, and Q4 deals slipped.
Asset services sensitivity to rates and collateral mix; rate direction could move yields either way.
Competitive intensity from new wealth entrants offering high RM payouts; RM attrition (regret attrition about 3-4% in Wealth).
Incremental asset management costs in FY27 for MF/SIF launch and new strategies.
Execution on SIF/MF license (final inspection done), private credit fund launch and RTA/trusteeship go-live by mid-Q3 FY27.
NII lag: loan book up 27% but NII growth lagged due to ECL provisioning; processing-fee acceleration expected in Q1 FY27.
Geopolitical volatility (West Asia) and the impact on ESOP-linked lending and client flows.

key_quotes: For us, it was a complete test of resilience this year. We navigated multiple moving parts, including something specific for us and overall macro uncertainty.
I don't think that this business one should rush in because one bad performance here can have years of negative impact.
I don't think the yield will compress because we've seen a decline in the overall interest rates happen and that flow-through has largely happened.
Next quarter, we could discuss the numbers. And by that time, maybe the volatility levels of the market also should settle down.
summary.management_tone: Management sounded confident on the wealth, private and asset services franchises, calling FY26 a growth year despite tariffs and the West Asia crisis. It was cautious on capital markets, describing ECM and QIP volumes as softer and Q4 deals as slipping. It was evasive on the exact yield outlook and gave no firm numbers on the SIF and mutual fund flows, deferring them to next quarter.

Private credit first fund, target INR1,000-1,500 crore, launch by end Q2 FY27
Domestic RTA and trusteeship services in Asset Services, go-live expected by mid-Q3 FY27

growth.why: Q4 revenue +7% YoY (+13% ex-IE and IB) and operating PAT +5%; FY27 growth rests on new fund launches (commercial real estate H2 FY27, private credit by end Q2 FY27), RTA go-live by mid-Q3 FY27, and wealth cost-to-income falling about 100 bps a year, with partial numeric backing but no explicit FY27 revenue guide.
